title: Oil Pressure Switch Replacement
introduction:
This replacement guide applies to the 2.3L EcoBoost engine. I use the large oil filter as a street sign: the pressure switch sits just above it in the drawings. The magenta connector identifies the electrical disconnection; the blue switch and discard symbol identify the part being replaced.

The job calls for hoist access, a new switch and controlled tightening during installation. It teaches replacement rather than an oil-pressure measurement, so completing it does not establish a pressure-test result.

items.name: Replacement switch
items.detail: Have a new oil pressure switch ready. The removed switch must be discarded.

items.name: Hoist and torque equipment
items.detail: Use a hoist suitable for the vehicle and torque equipment capable of applying the switch installation value given in the removal step.

items.name: Remote start and key
items.detail: Disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working underneath or around the vehicle. A remote start can cause personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service; an unexpected start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Auto start-stop, if equipped
items.detail: Keep the ignition off when servicing or working near rotating engine parts. An engine with auto start-stop may start automatically with the ignition on, causing serious personal injury.

items.name: Personal protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to use this protection may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Capacity and lifting points
items.detail: Confirm that hoist capacity covers the vehicle weight, including cargo and modifications. Use the lifting-point drawing in [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) and locate the triangles stamped into the unibody sheet metal or frame. Position the lift arms at the illustrated points. Lifting elsewhere can make the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury; incorrect hoist positioning can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Clearance around lift equipment
items.detail: Position adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering-linkage components to prevent damage. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped; also protect the axle and rear cover. Before driving onto a drive-on lift, check for interference that could damage the underbody.

items.name: Drive wheels
items.detail: Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are elevated off the ground. Drive wheels touching the ground can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Do not substitute the emergency jack
items.detail: The vehicle's supplied jack is only for an emergency deflated-tire change; using it for other work can damage the vehicle. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper, because the bumper covers will be damaged.

items.name: If a jack is used during vehicle handling
items.detail: Use a jack rated for the vehicle weight, including cargo and modifications, at the correct marked points on a hard, level surface. Set the parking brake and block wheels remaining on the ground. Support the vehicle on floor stands after jacking; never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, which can lower unexpectedly. Failure to secure and support the vehicle can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death. The replacement procedure itself specifies a hoist.

items.name: Before lifting and during lowering
items.detail: Start on a hard, level surface with the parking brake applied and wheels on the ground chocked. Keep the parking brake applied throughout this job, including when the specified transmission position is Neutral. Establish secure support on the hoist before going underneath. Before lowering, clear tools and people from the lowering area and confirm the parking brake remains applied. On an arm-type hoist, restore wheel chocks as the tires reach the ground before withdrawing the arms; on a drive-on lift, retain wheel restraints through lowering.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before refitting parts; they may also contain installation details.
edits.why: The switch tightening value is printed with removal but applies when the replacement is installed.

edits.text:
With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist using the specified lifting points and precautions.
Refer to: [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631) (100-02 Jacking and Lifting, Description and Operation).
edits.why: Hoist access is the required starting setup. I use the overview's underbody drawing and stamped triangle markers to locate the designated lifting points before positioning the lift arms.

edits.text: Disconnect the electrical connector from the oil pressure switch.
edits.why: The magenta connector is immediately above the large oil filter in the drawing. Disconnect it before removing the switch so the wiring is separated from the part being replaced.

edits.text:
Unscrew and remove the oil pressure switch, then discard it.
During installation, tighten the new switch to 133 lb.in (15 Nm).
edits.why: The blue highlight identifies the switch, and the discard symbol confirms that the removed part is not reused. The tightening value belongs to installation of its replacement.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: install a new oil pressure switch, tighten it to the value given above, reconnect its electrical connector, and lower the vehicle from the hoist.
edits.why: Reversing removal restores the new switch and its electrical connection while retaining the mandatory discard rule. Confirm the new switch has received its specified tightening and the connector is fully engaged before leaving the underside. Lower the vehicle with the restraints described in preparation; this is installation verification, not an oil-pressure measurement.
